subject: language
intro: I'm Ms. Kim. Let's plan a lesson on how dialogue drives a story forward.

beats.narration: The title is playful, and the lesson is about how talk moves the story.
This standard asks students to analyze how lines of dialogue propel action, reveal character, or provoke a decision.
Three functions of dialogue give students a clear lens.
beats.text: Students will be able to analyze how specific lines of dialogue propel the action, reveal character, or provoke a decision.

beats.narration: Acting it out makes dialogue come alive.
beats.text: Act out a short dialogue from a movie scene. "What did we learn about these characters just from how they talk?"

beats.narration: The three labels become a shared vocabulary.
beats.text: Model analyzing a dialogue-heavy scene, labeling each important line as propel, reveal, or provoke, and explaining why.

beats.narration: Rewriting a line shows how much a single line can change.
beats.text: Pairs choose a key dialogue scene from the class novel, label the lines, and then rewrite one line to change its function.

beats.narration: This matches the three-part lens directly.
beats.text: Choose one line of dialogue from today's reading. Does it propel, reveal, or provoke? Explain.

outro: Act it, model it, analyze it. Now plan yours.
